properties.displayName: T1090.001 - Internal Proxy - Port Forward or Tunnel
properties.description: Detects a host being set up as an internal proxy: a netsh portproxy rule (command or registry value), ssh/plink port forwarding, or a known tunnel tool such as chisel or ligolo. Built from purple team findings. Accounts allowed to use port forwarding are read from the DetectionExclusions watchlist (ExceptionType TunnelAccount).

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: Internal proxy: port forward or tunnel set up on {{DeviceName}}
alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{ReasonsText}}. Account: {{AccountName}}. Check what ran the command and where the forward or tunnel points, then look for other internal hosts sending traffic through this device.

properties.description: Detects one process relaying traffic: it accepts connections from internal hosts and connects onward, or holds an internet connection while reaching several internal endpoints. Limited to processes with no reason to relay traffic (rundll32, bare dllhost and similar) and rare programs in user-writable paths. Not exercised in the purple team test, so treat as unvalidated.

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: Internal proxy: process relaying traffic on {{DeviceName}}
alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{ReasonsText}}. Account: {{AccountName}}. Check what the process is and what started it, then which internal hosts connected through it.

properties.displayName: T1090.001 - Internal Proxy - C2 Named Pipe
properties.description: Detects peer-to-peer C2 over named pipes (SMB beacon style): a default C2 pipe name, or a pipe that accepts remote clients created by a process that should not host one, such as dllhost.exe started with no arguments. Built from purple team findings. SolarWinds Orion servers are read from the DetectionExclusions watchlist (ExceptionType OrionServer).

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: Internal proxy: suspicious C2 named pipe on {{DeviceName}}
alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{ReasonsText}}. Account: {{AccountName}}. Check what started the process and which hosts connected to the pipe, then look for the same pipe name on other devices.
